newsitem.title: CANADA: NHL ICE HOCKEY-CANADIENS BEAT LIGHTNING FOR THIRD STRAIGHT WIN.
newsitem.headline: NHL ICE HOCKEY-CANADIENS BEAT LIGHTNING FOR THIRD STRAIGHT WIN.

text.p: Brian Savage scored twice in a 80-second span to open the second period and Jocelyn Thibault turned aside 29 shots as the Montreal Canadiens won their third straight, beating the reeling Tampa Bay Lightning 4-2.
The Canadiens, who won three consecutive games for the first time since a four-game winning streak last April, received eight points from the line of Savage, Mark Recchi and Saku Koivu.
"Koivu was extraordinary, he's electrifying," Canadiens coach Mario Tremblay said. "That line can't play any better than they are. The way they pass the puck is unbelieveable."
"We are the same kind of players, we skate a lot, we play well together," Koivu said. "Sometimes there's no reason, but I'll take it."
Thibault was at his best over the opening 40 minutes, stopping 21 shots, including a breakaway by Daymond Langkow in the first period.
Rob Zamuner and Chris Gratton had a goal and an assist apiece for the Lightning, who have just two victories since October 22.

"Some of my players fell asleep for two minutes," Lightning coach Terry Crisp said. "We haven't played very well in the past 30 days, we should have had more victories. Some of those games we should have won. In six of our last eight games our players have been falling asleep for two minutes."
The Canadiens defeated Montreal for the the first time in their last five meetings and still trail the all-time series 4-8-2.

After a scoreless first period, Savage needed just six seconds to put Montreal on the board. Following the faceoff, Savage gathered in the loose puck, skated in on Tampa Bay goaltender Rick Tabaracci and beat him high to the stick side.
"It was a good goal to get us going. Somebody had to score," Savage said.
Just over a minute later, Recchi found Savage alone at the left post and he beat Tabaracci with a one-timer to the glove side for his 11th goal.
Tabaracci, making his first start since being acquired from Calgary last week, made 26 saves in falling to 2-5 on the season.

"Strange season, I played Montreal twice in this building and lost both times," Tabaracci said. "I think I played well tonight and we had great opportunities to score. The Canadiens are a gifted team with the nifty line of Recchi, Koivu and Savage."
Recchi notched his 12th of the season midway through the second period when he took a pass from Koivu and beat Tabaracci low to the stick side with a wrist shot.

Gratton got the Lightning on the board with 79 seconds left in the period. Zamuner slid a pass to Dino Cicarelli, who failed to get a shot off, and Gratton skated in and pushed the puck past Thibault.
Koivu and Zamuner exchanged third-period tallies, 22 seconds apart, to cap the scoring.
Montreal right wing Valeri Bure left the game during the first period and did not return after suffering a strained muscle in his neck.
